violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required. OBSERVED THE INTERIOR OF THE ICE MACHINE IN NEED OF CLEANING.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. ENSURE THE ICE MACHINE IS CLEANED TO THE SIGHT AND TOUCH BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: CUT LETTUCE (56 F), COOKED MUSHROOMS (54 F), COOKED ONIONS (54 F), AND CUT TOMATOES (56 F) ON A ICE BATH ON THE COUNTER AT THE COOK LINE FOR MORE THAN 4 HOURS.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth.CDI: ALL FOODS WERE DISCARDED.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoop in a container of water at 73 F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CDI: PIC REMOVED THE RICE SCOOP. PIC WILL STORE IN CONTAINER WITHOUT WATER MOVING FORWARD.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw fish was stored over cooked beef in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC moved the cooked beef to correct. CDI.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer

violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked onions that were 50°F were being held at room temperature. These onions were cooked at 12 PM.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The PIC was advised to discard the onions by 4 PM if they were not sold. CDI.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed. There were several foods in the walk-in refrigerator that had exceeded their expiration dates. These included containers of Cajun remoulade with an expiration date of 4/12, pimento cheese with an expiration date of 4/14, three containers of mayo sauce with an expiration date of 4/15, and a garlic product with an expiration date of 4/13.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. The PIC discarded all these products during the inspection to correct. CDI. Please be sure to monitor expiration dates of foods made on site and discard them when they exceed 7 days.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Raw vacuum packaged (Reduced Oxygen Packaging or ROP) frozen tuna was being thawed in the walk-in refrigerator, however, the packages were not cut open, as required.
violations.corrective_action: Ensure that frozen vacuum packed raw tuna packages are cut open to introduce oxygen and prevent the growth of anaerobic bacteria. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed several food stored on the floor in the walking refrigerator, including cases of potatoes and a container of food.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Discontinue storing food on floor refrigerator. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: there were two instances of in use utensils, being stored in standing water that was 75°F. One was on the rice cooker area, where the rice scoop was stored in standing water. The other was on the prep line area where knives and other equipment were stored in standing water. Also, there are a couple of businesses where bowls were being used to scoop foods out of storage containers.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Discontinue storing in-use utensils in standing water unless it is 135º and above at all times. Discontinue using bowls to scoop foods instead use handled utensils and keep the handles out of the foods. The PIC corrected these issues during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: The final sanitizing rinse concentration at the bar handsink was 0 parts per million chlorine.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. The PIC placed a service call for the unit and will use the warewashing machine in the kitchen, which was sanitizing properly. Please contact the EHS when the machine is working properly.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: a container of cooked butternut squash prepped on site had a prep date of October 21. There were several other containers of dressings and sauces with similar or older prep dates.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. Foods prepped on site and held more than 24 hours can only be held for 7 days. The EHS discussed this requirement with the PIC. The establishment has a 10-day shelf life for ready-to-eat prepared foods, which is not permitted. Please update the establishment procedures/policies to a 7-day shelf life for ready to eat foods prepared on site. The PIC discarded the butternut squash and other containers of foods with expiration dates that have exceeded 7 days.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure:
violations.corrective_action: There is a consumer advisory for all foods served raw or undercooked, however the asterisk for these foods are located in the wrong place. The asterisk must be next to the ingredient, not the menu item, that is served raw or undercooked. For example, the Turkey Rachel has an asterisk next to the name of the menu item. It is required that the asterisk be next to the ingredient that is raw or undercooked, not the name of the dish. In the above case, the creamy coleslaw or the secret sauce would need the asterisk, if they have raw or undercooked ingredients such as eggs. There are also a few menu items that don’t’ typically include raw or undercooked ingredients such as grilled cheese and chicken parm sub. Finally, the Kid’s Burger has an asterisk next to it. Children may not be served raw or undercooked ingredients such hamburgers at any time. Please plan on updating the menus and provide the EHS with a proof to review before printing so they can be reviewed for accuracy and compliance.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Vomiting and Diarrhea policy was provided during the inspection.
